If you don't use the models or watch the demos people post on social media, you may not realize there has been an astonishing jump in game development capability lately. We really are not that far away from a one-person game studio anymore.

You can mash up games now and the model will deliver a stable, playable fusion in one day. Some of them are so good that people don't post them openly online because they are afraid of getting sued. That's how quickly things have improved over the last few weeks with Astra and Opus 5.5.

Because of how virulently anti-AI the game industry has become, people are going to get completely blindsided by what's about to arrive. Not only are they unaware of how fast things are improving, they don't seem to understand the endgame. I see people taking about supply gluts, things like that.  This isn't about making games to sell on Steam and compete with the industry. If the player knows the type of game they want, and their model can code that game for them at the AAA level, in the genre they ask for, with the aesthetics and character design they prefer, then the question becomes: why buy a game from a studio at all?

I think Sir Demis sees this future with Genie. For the price of your subscription, you will get any style of game you want, tailored to you. Once that starts happening at scale, most game studios will very rapidly cease to exist. And that's the real endgame. Not competition; destruction. And it's closer than people think.

We asked Gemini Argon to teach the Apollo humanoid to play cornhole, and it zero-shotted it

All we gave it was a video of a person doing it. It then took control of the robot, generated its own sim env, performed some sysID, and trained launches on the real robot. 

It took it a few real shots to improve and then land many consecutive airmails. 

The process was so long and articulated that we asked the robot itself to explain what it did to us, as you can see at the end of the video. It even came up with the gestures

Special guest star, prinz:
Gemini
4 Argon is now available : )

Today we are rolling out Gemini 4 Argon globally in the Gemini API, to Pro + Ultra in Gemini App, and Ultra subs in Antigravity!

Argon is a huge step forward for Gemini, and a labor of love. This model has been battle tested by over 100,000 people at Google over the last month, with so much new innovation, ambition, and hard work baked into this release. The team has been heads down over the last 6 months working to make this possible across the stack (research, infra, safety, eng, etc).

We rolled the model out to cyber defenders as part of our fairwind program and early access customers over the last 2 weeks, it has been amazing to see and talk to folks who are now using this model daily. Seeing the models writing capability, raw knowledge and persistence for coding, paired with new features like 1M token output when the model needs to work more has gotten me even more excited about our path ahead.

This is just the start of the Gemini 4 era. As you saw with 3.5, 3.6, 3.7, and 3.8 Flash, our iteration speed with Gemini is fast : ) Now with Gemini 4 Argon to work from, I am cannot wait to see the progress continue, and most importantly see what this new model enables for the world. 

This is such a special moment in the arc of technology, as millions of people everyday tackle problems they could never have thought possible before. Gemini 4 Argon was built to help you tackle the hardest problems. I have personally felt this spark with Argon and hope you do too. Onwards!!
